title: Cap. VI Arg. 3: no Scripture tip for election from foresight faith — Si credideris, praedestinaberis?
pass_a_gloss: Now on the contrary, the adversaries cannot produce even one tip from the Scriptures by which it is hinted that men were elected before others from the foresighted condition of antecedent faith in them. But if the decree of predestining presupposes the condition of believing, and the election of the believer follows upon that condition fulfilled, this stipulation must be demonstrated from the sacred Scriptures. For to invent promises or covenants outside the word of God is the height of temerity. I ask therefore, Where is this promise found, If you shall have believed, you shall be predestined? Or, Whosoever shall have believed shall be predestined? There exists such a promise, Whosoever shall have believed shall be saved; because God requires the condition of faith as antecedent to decreed salvation: But there does not exist this, Whosoever shall have believed, or whosoever is foreseen as about to believe, shall be predestined; because God does not require faith as antecedent to his decree.
pass_b_english: On the other side, adversaries cannot produce so much as one tip of Scripture hinting that men were chosen above others from a foresighted condition of prior faith. If the predestining decree really presupposes believing, and election follows once that condition is met, that bargain must be shown from Holy Scripture — inventing promises outside God's word is sheer temerity. Where then is If you believe, you shall be predestined? Or Whoever believes shall be predestined? There is Whoever believes shall be saved — God requires faith as antecedent to decreed salvation. There is no Whoever believes (or is foreseen to believe) shall be predestined — God does not require faith as antecedent to his decree.
source_text: Jam e contra, adversarii ne unum quidem apicem ex Scripturis proferre possunt quo innuatur homines fuisse electos prae aliis ex praevisa antecedentis fidei in illis conditione. At si decretum praedestinandi praerequirat conditionem credendi, atque hac conditione impleta electio credentis consequatur, stipulatio haec ex sacris Scripturis est demonstranda. Nam fingere promissiones aut pacta extra verbum Dei est summae temeritatis. Quaero igitur, Ubi habetur haec promissio, Si credideris, praedestinaberis? Vel, Quicunque crediderint, praedestinabuntur? Extat promissio talis, Quisquis crediderit, salvabitur; quia Deus exigit conditionem fidei tanquam antecedaneum ad salutem decretam: At non extat haec, Quisquis crediderit, aut quisquis praevidetur crediturus, praedestinabitur; quia Deus non exigit fidem tanquam antecedaneum ad suum decretum.
